title: Execution of the Endpoint-Stack Pop Routine
statement: Let $E$ and $B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four decider indices and Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $b$ be a Boolean phase. For a machine register state $st$, suppose its loop counter, time scratch register, copy-and-shift scratch register, pop scratch register, and popped-endpoint register are all zero; every register is at most $B$; and its saved-endpoints stack has value $q2^{st.w}+e$, where $q,e$ are natural numbers and $e<2^{st.w}$. Starting with state $st$, no recorded answer, and the instruction that begins popping the saved endpoint for phase $b$, the abstract machine reaches the instruction that increments the level for phase $b$, with the saved-endpoints stack changed to $q$, the popped-endpoint register changed to $e$, all other registers unchanged, and no answer recorded. Every configuration before the final one satisfies the program guard with bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is an oracle on four deciders and Boolean words
the time scratch register is zero
the copy-and-shift scratch register is zero
the pop scratch register is zero
every register of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Fix a natural number $E$, an oracle on four deciders and Boolean-string inputs, an input
string $x$, and a natural-number register bound $B$. For either phase bit $b$, suppose a
machine state has counter $C$, scratch registers $T,Z,Q$, and endpoint register $E$ all
equal to zero; all its registers are at most $B$; and its endpoint stack has the form
$q2^w+e$ with $e<2^w$. Then the machine starting at the pop routine for phase $b$, with
this state and no answer recorded, reaches the state at the increment-level instruction
with the same registers except that the endpoint stack is $q$ and the endpoint register
is $e$, with no answer recorded; throughout the run, each visited configuration
satisfies the guard requiring the program’s precondition and all registers to be at most
$B$.
